facts.text: Bath was laid out in 1903 when the railroad reached the spot, earning it the nickname New Bath to avoid confusion with Old Bath.
Bath sits in Bath Township, an unincorporated community within Franklin County, Indiana.
From March 1 to July 31, the Legends & Landmarks event invites residents to explore Wabash County’s rich history as part of America’s 250th anniversary.
Wabash County’s lodging options range from historic hotels and converted horse stables to charming bed‑and‑breakfasts and primitive campsites.
Tourists can uncover a hidden letter by visiting all 19 historical sites in Wabash County, each revealing a clue to the next.
